notes.text: A noisy last-symbol detector. Each read moves to the state matching the symbol 90% of the time and the wrong way 10% of the time — a channel that garbles one bit in ten. The language is still exactly "ends in a", because the accepting mass lands on 0.9 or 0.1 and the cut-point λ = 0.5 sits between them.

Watch the Pr row: unlike an NFA's set of states, a PFA carries a probability per state, and every (state, symbol) row sums to 1. The verdict compares the accepting mass against λ — strictly greater accepts. Because 0.9 and 0.1 stay well clear of 0.5, the cut-point is isolated and the language stays regular.

meta.title: Noisy channel: does it end in a?
meta.blurb: A two-state probabilistic automaton over a 10% noisy channel. The accepting mass is 0.9 after an a and 0.1 after a b, so cut-point 0.5 recovers the language "ends in a" despite the noise.
